verdict.rationale: Fedora is a free, open-source distro that can be installed on generic x86 hardware without vendor tie-in, and community reports confirm it 'works best out of the box' on varied hardware (fedora-comm-6), but the same threads flag real hardware friction—NVIDIA driver/suspend issues, Wi‑Fi problems, and Wayland breaking on older machines (fedora-comm-6, fedora-comm-8, fedora-comm-19)—showing hardware freedom is not friction-free. Missing for 10: explicit vendor documentation on hardware certification/compatibility lists, ARM/other-architecture support claims, and independent benchmarks confirming broad hardware compatibility beyond anecdotal forum comments.
